Down the

[Verse 1]
[E]street you can hear her scream "you're a disgrace" As she
[G#m]slams the door in his drunken face, And
[D#m7]now he stands outside and all the
[E]neighbors start to [B]gossip and
[F#]drool.
He
[E]cries "Oh girl, you must be mad, What

[F#]garden green.
And so

[G#m7]in the sea, e-

A little

[Verse 2]
[E]Indian brave who before he was ten, played
[G#m]war games in the woods with his Indian friends, and he
[D#m7]built a dream that when he grew up, he would
[E]be a fearless [B]warrior
[F#]Indian Chief.
Many
[E]moons passed and more the dream grew strong, until to-
[G#m]morrow He would sing his first war song, And
[D#m7]fight his first battle, but something went wrong, sur-
[E]prise attack [B]killed
[F#]him in his sleep that night
And so

[Chorus]
[A#m7]castles made of sand, melts
[G#m7]into the sea e-
[F#]ventually.

[Solo]
[F#]
There

[Verse 3]
[E]was a young girl, whose heart was a frown, Because
[G#m]she was crippled for life, and couldn't speak a sound And she
[D#m7]wished and prayed she would stop
[E]living, [B]so she de-
[F#]cided to die.
She drew
[E]wheel chair to the edge of the shore, and to
[G#m]her legs she smiled "You won't hurt me no more." But
[D#m7]then a sight she'd never seen made her jump and say
[E]"Look, a [B]golden winged
[F#]ship is passing my way"
And it really didn't
have to stop it just kept on going.

[Chorus]
[A#m7]And so castles
[G#m7]made of sand
[F#]slips into the sea, E-
ventually
